name: Kwajongen (Troeven)
description: Kwajongen (Flemish for 'Bad Boy' or 'Naughty Boy') is a regional trick-taking game popular in Flanders, particularly in Belgian Limburg. It is the Flemish equivalent of the Walloon game 'Couillon'. Played with a 24-card deck by four players in partnerships, it is a game of quick calculation where teams compete to 'erase' points from a starting score (often visualized as lines on a chalkboard or branches on a tree).

content.text: Kwajongen (Flemish for 'Bad Boy' or 'Naughty Boy') is a regional trick-taking game popular in Flanders, particularly in Belgian Limburg. It is the Flemish equivalent of the Walloon game 'Couillon'. Played with a 24-card deck by four players in partnerships, it is a game of quick calculation where teams compete to 'erase' points from a starting score (often visualized as lines on a chalkboard or branches on a tree).
Part of the broader European Jass and Couillon tradition. It became a distinct regional marker of Flemish identity, especially in the mining communities of Limburg.
24 cards (standard ranks 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace).
